subject: Quick follow-up: scheduling demo & security intake
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@finanova.com>, Paul Jensen <paul.j@finanova.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-03-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Quick follow-up: scheduling demo & security intake

Thanks again for the call this morning — really helpful to hear more about Finanova's fraud-detection pipeline and where latency and cost are becoming blockers. Recap and suggested next steps below: 

Recap (2 bullets):
- Primary goal: reduce tail latency on 1–2s inference paths while keeping unit-cost per token under your current budget.
- Key stakeholders: you (product), Paul (procurement), and a security engineer for SSO/data flow review.

Proposed next steps (please pick one):
1) 30-minute product demo (high-level use cases, success metrics) — ~30 minutes
   Options: Tue 2028-03-06 10:00 AM PST or Wed 2028-03-07 2:00 PM PST
2) 60-minute technical deep dive (SSO, data controls, latency tuning, KV cache demo) — ~60 minutes
   Options: Tue 2028-03-06 11:30 AM PST or Thu 2028-03-08 9:00 AM PST

Pre-call asks for the technical deep dive:
- If you want SSO/SSO metadata discussed, please loop in your security engineer (email or name) so we can include concrete runbook items.
- If procurement wants a short pre-call to cover terms/pricing cadence, we can schedule a 15-minute sync the day prior.

Attached: SOC2_summary.pdf and initial-quote-FN-0456.pdf for visibility.

If you reply with preferred time(s), I’ll lock calendar invites and loop our platform engineer (Karithik) and Rishi from accounts for procurement details.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0123

Procurement note: Paul asked for a 15-min procurement scoping call to go over payment terms and initial SLAs — can we do a quick call on Mon 2028-03-05 at 11:00 AM PST? If that works, I’ll send the calendar invite and include our legal contact as needed.

Security/technical asks (so your team can prepare):
- SSO types supported (SAML/OIDC) + example metadata file
- Data retention and log export options (audit/logging frequency)
- Any available benchmark data for 30/100/300 token tails

Thanks — looping Maya from security for any additional asks.
